blocks.html: An anonymous letter to the well-beloved Gaius

items.html: The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth.

blocks.html:
From the elder to the well-beloved Gaius, [1]

whom I truly love.

items.html: Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.
For I rejoiced greatly, when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth.
I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.

blocks.html: Beloved, I hope your body is as healthy as your soul.

items.html: Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers;
Which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well:
Because that for his name's sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles.
We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth.

blocks.html:
Beloved, you faithfully do whatever you do

to friends and stangers.

I'll remember Diotrephes

(for saying bad things about us)

items.html: I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.

blocks.html:
I wrote to the church, but Diotrephes,

who likes to be honored, didn't receive us.

items.html: Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth, prating against us with malicious words: and not content therewith, neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church.

blocks.html:
If I come I'll remember what he did,

saying bad things about us.
Those who do good are of God

items.html: Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.
Demetrius hath good report of all men, and of the truth itself: yea, and we also bear record; and ye know that our record is true.

blocks.html:
Beloved, do good, avoid evil.

Whoever does good is of God.

Whoever does evil hasn't seen God. [2]

items.html: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee:
But I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to thee. Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name.

blocks.html:
but I'll tell you when I see you face to face.

Say hi to everyone.

footnotes.html:
The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius (v.1)

The author of this letter does't identifying himself, except to say he's an elder.

Presumably, the elder is the same guy who pretended to be the apostle John in the first two Johannine epistles.

No one knows who the "Gaius" guy was either.

He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God. (v.11)

Do Christians sin?

Does anyone ever do anything good?
